note: Life-event journeys. Every step must reference a real service id from data/service-index.json; fees and processing times are NOT stored here, they are read from that index at render time. Each journey has exactly one owning category - other categories listing it in relatedCategories show a referral card, not the full journey. Draft copy and reviewer notes live in docs/journeys-draft.md.

journeys.title: I'm building a house
journeys.summary: Two offices, in this order. The building permit can't be filed until City Planning has cleared the location, and the location can't be cleared until you know how the lot is zoned.

steps.label: Check what your lot is zoned for
steps.note: A site zoning or land use certification tells you whether a house is allowed there at all.

steps.label: Get locational clearance for the building permit
steps.note: City Planning confirms the plan fits the zoning before the engineers will look at it.

steps.label: Apply for the building permit
steps.note: The long one - 16 documentary requirements.

steps.label: Apply for the electrical permit
steps.note: Filed alongside the building permit at the same window, not after it.

steps.label: Get the certificate of occupancy
steps.note: Once built. You are not allowed to occupy the building without it.

journeys.title: I'm subdividing or developing land
journeys.summary: All at City Planning, but budget for two months if the land needs reclassifying first.

steps.label: Confirm the current land use
steps.note: What the land is zoned for today.

steps.label: Reclassify the land, if it isn't zoned for what you plan
steps.note: The step people don't expect, and the one that sets the timeline. Skip it if the land is already zoned for your use.

steps.label: Apply for preliminary approval and locational clearance
steps.note: The subdivision approval itself.

journeys.title: I'm holding an event on a public road
journeys.summary: A fiesta procession, motorcade, recorrida or fun run. Three separate permits, all at the City Engineer's Office - the banners are charged separately from the road.

steps.label: Get the road use permit
steps.note: To close or use a city road for the activity.

steps.label: Get a permit for your banners and tarpaulins
steps.note: Separate from the road permit, and charged by size and duration.

steps.label: Get a truck ban exemption, if you're bringing floats or heavy vehicles
steps.note: Only if your event needs trucks on city roads during truck ban hours.

journeys.title: I'm opening a business
journeys.summary: Four offices. City Planning clears the location, BPLO issues the permit, the Treasurer collects, and the City Engineer inspects the premises.

steps.label: Get locational clearance for the site
steps.note: City Planning confirms your address is zoned for the business you intend to run. The zoning fee is folded into BPLO's one-time assessment.

steps.label: Apply for the new business permit
steps.note: At the office. There is an online route as well - see the section below.

steps.label: Pay the business tax and permit fees
steps.note: At the One-Stop Shop, against the order of payment BPLO assesses.

steps.label: Get the annual inspection certificate
steps.note: The City Engineer inspects the premises. Large or complex establishments take longer.

journeys.title: I'm renewing my business permit
journeys.summary: Shorter than a new application, but still three offices. Renewals run in January, when the queues are longest.

steps.label: Get locational clearance for the renewal
steps.note: Confirms nothing about the site has changed since last year.

steps.label: File the renewal
steps.note: The Priority, Express and Bulk lanes exist for this - which one you use depends on your requirements.

steps.label: Pay the assessed business tax
steps.note: Against the order of payment issued at filing.

journeys.title: We're starting a cooperative
journeys.summary: The Cooperative Development Office runs the whole path, but the seminars come before the paperwork, not after.

steps.label: Request an orientation
steps.note: Where the office explains what forming a cooperative commits you to.

steps.label: Complete the Pre-Membership Education Seminar
steps.note: Required of your members before registration will be endorsed.

steps.label: Get your registration endorsed
steps.note: The city endorses; the Cooperative Development Authority registers.

steps.label: Get an endorsement for the cooperative's business permit
steps.note: Only once the cooperative is registered and trading.

journeys.title: Someone in my family has died
journeys.summary: Register within 30 days - after that it becomes a delayed registration with more requirements. The Mayor's Office also has burial assistance.

steps.label: Register the death within 30 days
steps.note: Past 30 days this becomes a delayed registration, which asks for more.

steps.label: Get certified copies of the death certificate
steps.note: Banks, insurers and the courts will each want their own.

steps.label: Endorse the record to the PSA
steps.note: So a PSA copy can be issued anywhere in the country, not only here.

steps.label: Ask the Mayor's Office about burial assistance
steps.note: Medical, burial and financial assistance are handled together at the City Mayor's Office.

journeys.title: I've had a baby
journeys.summary: Register within 30 days. The PSA endorsement is the step people forget, and it's the one that lets you get a copy anywhere in the country.

steps.label: Register the birth within 30 days
steps.note: After 30 days it becomes a delayed registration, with more requirements.

steps.label: File for the child to use the father's surname
steps.note: Only if the parents are not married and you want the father's surname on the record.

steps.label: Get a certified copy of the birth certificate
steps.note: Schools and passports will ask for it.

steps.label: Endorse the record to the PSA
steps.note: So a PSA copy can be issued outside Legazpi.

journeys.title: We're getting married
journeys.summary: The licence comes first and takes time to release. Registering the marriage afterwards is a separate visit.

steps.label: Apply for the marriage licence
steps.note: Apply well before the date - the licence is not issued the same day.

steps.label: Register the marriage
steps.note: After the ceremony. The solemnising officer files, but the record is registered here.

steps.label: Get a certified copy of the marriage certificate
steps.note: Needed for name changes, benefits and immigration.

journeys.title: I'm looking for work
journeys.summary: PESO is the front door. Which programme fits depends on whether you're a student, a first-time jobseeker, or between jobs.

steps.label: Register as a jobseeker
steps.note: Job matching and referrals to employers hiring through PESO.

steps.label: Join JobStart, if you're a first-time jobseeker
steps.note: Life skills and technical training with a paid internship.

steps.label: Ask about TUPAD, GIP or DILEEP
steps.note: DOLE grant-based programmes for emergency employment and livelihood.

journeys.title: I want to work for the city
journeys.summary: A different office from the one that helps jobseekers. Human Resource Management handles city posts, from application to your certificate of employment years later.

steps.label: Apply for a city post
steps.note: Recruitment, selection and placement for vacancies at the city.

steps.label: Have your appointment or contract prepared
steps.note: Contracts of service, job orders and appointments are all prepared here.

steps.label: Request a certificate of employment when you need one
steps.note: For loans, visas or a new employer.

journeys.title: I'm hiring
journeys.summary: PESO recruits on an employer's behalf at no charge, and runs the student and grant programmes that subsidise some hires.

steps.label: Register as an employer with PESO
steps.note: PESO refers matched jobseekers to you.

steps.label: Hire students through SPES
steps.note: The Special Program for the Employment of Students, for seasonal work.

steps.label: Take on a JobStart intern
steps.note: Trainees complete their internship with a partner employer.

journeys.title: My business needs an Environmental Certificate
journeys.summary: A seminar, then the certificate. You can attend in person or online - the two routes are separate services with different processing times.

steps.label: Attend the environmental seminar in person
steps.note: For a new certificate or a renewal.

steps.label: Or attend the same seminar online
steps.note: The webinar route, if you'd rather not attend in person.

steps.label: Take the non-compliant route, if your certificate lapsed
steps.note: A separate seminar for businesses whose certificate has expired.

journeys.title: I need waste or a septic tank dealt with
journeys.summary: Desludging is requested directly. Hauling anything to the landfill yourself needs a permit first.

steps.label: Request septic tank desludging
steps.note: For households and establishments.

steps.label: Get a Permit to Dump, if you're hauling waste yourself
steps.note: Required before the city disposal facility will accept your load.

steps.label: Get a visitor's pass for the Sanitary Landfill Facility
steps.note: For site visits and research, not for disposal.

journeys.title: I want to plant, or cut, a tree
journeys.summary: Seedlings are free. Cutting a tree - even on your own land - needs a certificate of no objection first.

steps.label: Request free tree seedlings
steps.note: For households, schools, barangays and organisations.

steps.label: Get a Certificate of No Objection before cutting a tree
steps.note: Required before any tree is cut, including on private property.

steps.label: Get a certification to register a chainsaw
steps.note: Chainsaws must be registered, and registration needs this certification first.

journeys.title: I need a relocation slot
journeys.summary: The application comes first. The utility certification is what actually gets power and water connected once you're there.

steps.label: Apply for a slot in a relocation site
steps.note: For families qualified under the city's resettlement programme.

steps.label: Ask about financial assistance after an eviction
steps.note: Support for families displaced by demolition or eviction.

steps.label: Get the certification for an ALECO or LCWD connection
steps.note: The utilities will not connect a relocation address without it.

journeys.title: I want to buy a city lot through socialized housing
journeys.summary: A city-owned lot sold under the socialized housing programme, not on the open market.

steps.label: Apply to buy a city-owned lot
steps.note: Through the socialized housing programme.

steps.label: Have a subdivision plan or scheme prepared
steps.note: The office prepares the plan for the lot being conveyed.

steps.label: Request any certification the sale needs
steps.note: Certifications the Assessor or Registry of Deeds asks for.

journeys.title: We're forming a homeowners' association
journeys.summary: The office assists with formation, and issues the certifications an association needs afterwards.

steps.label: Get help forming the association
steps.note: The office assists residents through formation and organisation.

steps.label: Request the certifications the association needs
steps.note: For registration and for dealings with national agencies.

steps.label: Request a meeting with a national agency
steps.note: The office arranges meetings with HLURB, NHA and others on residents' behalf.

journeys.title: I need financial or medical assistance
journeys.summary: The certificate of indigency is the document most assistance depends on, so it comes first. Two offices offer help and they are not the same programme.

steps.label: Get a certificate of indigency
steps.note: With the social case study and assessment report that go with it.

steps.label: Apply for assistance to individuals in crisis (AICS)
steps.note: Limited financial assistance for medical, burial and other crisis situations.

steps.label: Ask the Mayor's Office about its own assistance
steps.note: A separate programme from AICS, for medical, burial and financial help.

steps.label: Get the PhilHealth certification of financial incapacity
steps.note: For Universal Health Care coverage of a hospital bill.

journeys.title: I need a PWD ID
journeys.summary: One application covers the ID and both booklets - the medicine booklet and the purchase booklet that carry the discounts.

steps.label: Apply for the PWD ID, medicine booklet and purchase booklet
steps.note: All three are issued together by the Persons with Disability Affairs Office.

steps.label: Get a certificate of indigency, if you're also applying for assistance
steps.note: Most welfare assistance depends on this document.

journeys.title: Someone I know needs help with drug dependency
journeys.summary: The council handles this as a health and community matter. Asking a question first costs nothing and commits no one.

steps.label: Ask the council a question
steps.note: Before anything formal starts.

steps.label: Arrange a drug test
steps.note: Through the council rather than privately.

steps.label: Join the community-based intervention programme
steps.note: The city's own programme, run in the community rather than a facility.

journeys.title: I'm buying or selling property
journeys.summary: Two offices, and the order matters - the Treasurer assesses and collects the transfer tax before the Assessor will move the tax declaration to the new owner.

steps.label: Have the transfer tax assessed
steps.note: The Treasurer computes what is due on the sale.

steps.label: Pay the transfer tax
steps.note: Against the assessment.

steps.label: Transfer the tax declaration to the new owner
steps.note: At the Assessor's Office. The property stays in the seller's name until this is done.

steps.label: Get a real property tax clearance
steps.note: Proof that nothing is owed on the property.

journeys.title: I've built something and need it declared
journeys.summary: A new house, building or machine has to be declared with the Assessor before it can be taxed - and it will be taxed from the year it was completed.

steps.label: Declare the new house, building or machine
steps.note: The Assessor inspects and assesses it for tax purposes.

steps.label: Request the real property tax statement of account
steps.note: What is now due on the property.

steps.label: Pay the real property tax
steps.note: Annually, or quarterly if you prefer.

journeys.title: I'm paying my business tax
journeys.summary: Get the billing statement, have it assessed, then pay. Delinquencies from previous years are assessed separately.

steps.label: Request the quarterly billing statement
steps.note: What is due this quarter.

steps.label: Have the business tax assessed
steps.note: The Treasurer computes the amount.

steps.label: Settle any previous-year delinquency
steps.note: Assessed separately from the current year's tax.

steps.label: Pay the business tax
steps.note: At the One-Stop Shop or through the online billing portal.

journeys.title: I'm registering as a farmer or fisherfolk
journeys.summary: RSBSA registration comes first - it's what most support and insurance depends on. Inputs and advice follow from it.

steps.label: Register in RSBSA, PCIC insurance or boat registration
steps.note: The national registry of farmers and fisherfolk, plus crop insurance and boat registration.

steps.label: Request technical advice or a farm visit
steps.note: Agri-fishery advice, site visitation and capacity-building.

steps.label: Request seeds, seedlings, fertilizer or fingerlings
steps.note: Distribution of production inputs to registered farmers.

journeys.title: I need farm machinery
journeys.summary: The Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering division advises, lends and registers. Machinery you own has to be registered whether or not you borrow from the city.

steps.label: Get advice on farm structures, machines or irrigation
steps.note: Includes a field visit and ocular inspection of your site.

steps.label: Borrow pre- and postharvest machinery
steps.note: City-owned machinery lent to registered farmers and associations.

steps.label: Register machinery you own
steps.note: Farm and fishery machinery must be registered.

steps.label: Request a training or seminar on farm machinery
steps.note: For farmers' associations and cooperatives.

journeys.title: I have pets or livestock
journeys.summary: Dogs and cats are pre-registered at the barangay before the city's rabies vaccination reaches them. Travelling with a pet needs a health certificate.

steps.label: Pre-register your dogs and cats at the barangay
steps.note: The list the city works from when vaccination comes round.

steps.label: Have them vaccinated during the mass rabies vaccination
steps.note: Run by the City Veterinary Office across the barangays.

steps.label: Get a veterinary health certificate to travel with a pet
steps.note: Airlines and shipping lines will ask for it.

steps.label: Ask for a farm or home visit
steps.note: For livestock and animals that cannot be brought in.
